description:
FILED s509+ (Fable, 2026-10-06) from probing the cases in https://perlmonks.org/index.pl?node_id=44722 ("On Parsing Perl") for a reddit answer.  Probed vs perl 5.40.3 at main ad1ede72.

PPI decides `/` after a bareword is DIVISION, then ends the statement at the next `;` and starts a comment at the next `#` -- so the closing `/` of the match is in ANOTHER statement or inside a Comment token, where `_repair_word_match` (#351, #872, #484) does not look.

  $_ = "x 25 ; # y";
  sin  / 25 ; # / ; die "regex";     perl: dies (sin(/ 25 ; # /))   PCL: no die -- sin()/25, SILENT WRONG
  my @r = (sin /;/, 9);               perl: 0.84.. 9                   PCL: statement DROPPED (loud; dies there)
  sub one {...}  my $v = one /a;b # x/;  perl: one(1)                   PCL: "Illegal division by zero" (one() / a)

PPI dump of line 1: Statement[Word sin, Operator /, Number 25, Structure ;] + Comment `# / ; die "x";`.

RIGHT TODAY (same probe session, all identical to perl): `time / 25 ; # / ; die` (division), `split /,/`, `sin /foo/`, `FOO / 7` (use constant), `no_args / 25` (declared ()), an IMPORTED () sub `aaa / 25`, `one_arg /foo/`, `normal /o,b/, 2`, imported `bbb /foo/`, `BEGIN { *zzz = sub () { 42 } } zzz / 2`.

SIZE: the shape is rare outside deliberately adversarial code (a match with a `;` or ` #` in it, written without parens after a word that takes arguments).  Not scheduled.  The cheap discriminating measurement before any fix: count the shape over the four populations -- a repair candidate is a Statement ending `WORD-that-is-not-a-term / ... ;` whose following siblings (to end of LINE, comment included) hold an unescaped `/`.  A fix belongs with the other token repairs (re-lex the line from the `/`), and it gets a ppi-upstream-bugs.md section only if PPI could know better -- for a BUILTIN that takes an argument (sin) it could; for a user sub it cannot.

SIBLING, noted in #2610: `BEGIN { eval q{sub zzz () { 42 }} } print zzz / 2` -> perl 21, PCL 0 (the name is unknown when the file is parsed, so it reads as the string "zzz").

ADDED same day (the reddit thread, r/perl 1wz2p7a -- the asker is merlyn himself; the other operator-or-term characters probed after a constant vs after an arg-taking sub: `% & * < << - + . {` and `x` ALL identical to perl).  One more member, LOUD: an EMPTY pattern after an arg-taking user sub -- `sub args {...}  print "x ", (args //, 2)` -> perl `x args(1 2)`, PCL drops the statement ("Handle single node of unknown type"; PPI lexes `//` as defined-or).  `split //, $s`, a bare `//` in a condition and `$u // 4` are right.
subject: A regex after a WORD whose body holds `;` or `#` is cut by PPI at that character, and the #351 `WORD /` repair works inside ONE statement: `sin / 25 ; # / ; die` is silently DIVISION (merlyn, PerlMonks 44722)
